# Feature: Game engine refactor: kernel + packs

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Refactor the monolithic PixiJS game into a deterministic kernel plus internal pack (mod-style) registry per plans/game-engine-refactor/REFACTOR.md, so novel mechanics are added as one pack file + level data + one test room. Preserve pure step(state,input) determinism, session replay/fork, existing level JSON, and all shipped mechanics.

## User Story

**As a** developer adding novel mechanics
**I want** mechanics isolated as packs on a small kernel
**So that** new features cost less to implement and review than editing monolithic files.

## High-Level Use Case

Developer registers tile/item definitions and step hooks in a pack file by namespaced ID (core:orb, keys:key-red, core:warp). Kernel runs the fixed pipeline input->intent->move->terrain->objects->links->tick->win/lose arbitration. Renderer and HUD only read state + definitions. Levels up to 64x64 scroll with a renderer-only camera.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given any existing level and input log, per-step observable readout (position, inventory, orbs, status, timer) is unchanged.
- Given keys/locks pack disabled, only keys/locks stop working; floor/walls/timer still play.
- Given a level larger than the viewport (up to 64x64), the camera centres on the player and clamps; small levels render identically.
- Given water without flippers, the player loses; with flippers, water is safe (kept proof pack).

## Edge Cases & Rules

- State shape versions once to state.v=2; old sessions are discarded (human decision 2026-10-30), inputs still define replay within a version.
- Win and lose requested in the same step: lose wins unless the run was already won.
- Terrain-effect chains (ice/force) are bounded so a step always terminates.
- Inventory cap stays 8; unknown level chars are load errors.

## UI / Feedback

- HUD values come from pack-registered readouts (time/orbs/level/inventory); no mechanic strings in kernel or HUD helpers.
- Camera movement is smooth/centred on player; HUD right column unchanged on small levels.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- No new sprites required; reuse level-sprites and gui-sprites. Water/flipper tiles in Phase 5 reuse existing sprite pipeline (fallback tile acceptable for test room).
- New test levels: scroll-room (large, <=64x64), water-room.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Kernel grep gate reports zero mechanic-specific strings/branches.
- [ ] Regression corpus: identical per-step readout on all levels vs pre-refactor baseline.
- [ ] test_keys_and_locks.py passes with keys/locks as a pack; pack-disable isolation check passes.
- [ ] test_orbs_and_gate, test_level_timer, test_warp_and_levels pass via core pack (core:warp naming).
- [ ] 64x64-class level scrolls; existing rooms render identically.
- [ ] Water/flippers pack kept and removable as two files.
- [ ] Full suite green: python3 -m unittest discover -s tools, plus browser play/replay smoke.

## Out of Scope

- No external mod support/sandboxing, build step, TypeScript, framework, or ECS library.
- No changes to tools/server.py, PM tool, asset tool, or level file format (loader shims absorb differences).
- No pushing/monsters implementation (design accommodates them only).
- No support beyond 64x64 levels.

## Open Questions

None. Human decisions 2026-10-30: max level 64x64; exit named warp (core:warp), orbs stay orbs; discard old sessions at state.v=2; keep water/flippers pack.

## Testing

Mechanics playgrounds: reuse all existing test rooms plus new scroll-room and water-room. Regression corpus (Phase 0) is the primary evidence; record agent play sessions for replay on playable phases.
